title.narrative: Envelope 12: Enhancing access to equitable life saving and life‐sustaining comprehensive services through complementary Protection, WASH and FSL assistance in IDPs camps in Idleb

description.narrative: The proposed project is protection centered with integrated and complementarity through providing services complementing other sectors in all sites, Protection services will provided in all locations, FSLampWaSH will be provided based on needs amp gaps and will complement already running projects( SCHF22028-21950) and other services providers such as SHAFAK amp IHH where we will provide FSL in WaSH supported camps and vice versa, to support Vulnerable groups in 25 IDPs camps in Dana and Maaret Tamsrin through Protection, WaSH and FSL interventions serving around 45,091 (M 9433, W 10670, B 12360, G 12628) from the most vulnerable IDPs of men, women, boys and girls focusing on PWD, (9500 household). Protection: intervention designed to increase resilience of PWD especially women and girls, as well as CP through community participation utilizing outreach modality which will focus on improving resilience through set of prevention and response activities to mitigate protection risks, the proposed intervention will be implemented via conducting psychosocial support for PWD and their family members, structured PSS, problem management (PM+) which affect positively the beneficiary's social network and strengthening positive lifestyle. In addition to community’s active participation to prevent and respond to CP issues, engaging educational sites amp camps to build disability inclusion capacity through conducting accessibility audits in targeted locations, and child resilience activities, training amp awareness sessions on inclusion, beneficiaries will benefit of IPA,CP services, referrals, and access to socio-economic activities. To increase awareness and decrease the risks of SEA, PSEA training will be provided for 200 humanitarian workers, while 6 PSEA Facilitators will conduct awareness sessions for beneficiaries and community members. WASH: intervention designed to improve access to safe water and sanitation in IDPs camps in Dana. In total 16,703 IDPs will benefit from WASH services including water network, solar system, sewage network, Cholera hygiene promotion and other WASH services, WASH intervention will target camps by extension and rehabilitation of WASH infrastructure (extension of water network, solar system, and sewage network) in Nasem Al Khair and Shuhada Al Insaniya camps and connect them to water station. Also another WaSH intervention will provide elevated water tanks in Al Faraj and Khaled Ibn Al Walid camps and connecting it to Wadi Abbas water station. Water quality will be ensured, and water will be chlorinated with FRC between 0.5 - 0.7. Sewage network in Shuhada Al Insaniya camp will be constructed, the WASH component will provide full WaSH package including solid waste management, desludging and conducting hygiene promotion campaigns focusing on cholera and personal hygiene including distribution of soap. The project also will continue the support of Al Ahmar and Muhajari Kansafra stations (under SCHF 22028) that benefit 6 camps starting in April, FSL:integrated interventions is designed to improve food security as one of the most urgent needs of the most vulnerable communities under this allocation, HIHFAD will purchase 400 MT of flour from the local Market, this flour will be processed via contracting local bakeries to produce 460 MT of fresh bread bundles (1 KG) to be distributed to about 3900 IDPs HHs using in-kind modality in 23 identified camps, 10 camps in Dana and 13 camps in Maaret Tamsrin. The IDPs in 17 Camps will start receiving bread bundles in April because they are currently covered from (SCHF 22028), and the IDPs in 6 Camps will start receiving bread starting from March as they are currently not covered. 6 camps will be selected in coordination with FSL Cluster,distribution will target all the IDPs in all selected camps as a blanket distribution for 26 days per month for 4 months. 160 BBs per HHs to 1500 HHs who will receive in March and 96 BBs per HHs to 2400 HHs who will receive in April 2023.
